assigner is maturing, and some change is inevitable as methods are evaluated
and improved. Functions are considered stable unless their documentation says
otherwise.

## Experimental functions

The following functions are available for use, but remain experimental:

- `assign_individuals()`;
- `amova_genomic()`;
- `assign_likelihood_dapc()`;
- `compare_unsampled_scores()`; and
- `assess_assignment_mc()`.

Their interfaces, numerical or validation strategies, and returned components
may change. Results produced with these functions should therefore be tied to
both the assigner version and, for a development installation, the exact Git
commit.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Record the installed package version.
utils::packageVersion("assigner")

# GitHub installations made with common R installation tools may retain the
# source commit in the installed package metadata.
description <- utils::packageDescription("assigner")
description[c("Version", "RemoteSha")]

# When working directly from an assigner source checkout, record its commit.
system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE)
```

`RemoteSha` is not present in every installation. When it is absent, record the
commit from the source checkout or the immutable GitHub commit URL used for the
installation. Saving `sessionInfo()` with the analysis is also recommended.

This terminology follows the lifecycle guidance in *R Packages (2e)*:
<https://r-pkgs.org/lifecycle.html>.
